fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Keep the single driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the residence without obstruction.
• Install a turnaround area or ensure sufficient space near the residence for emergency vehicles to reverse out without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Mark the location of the water feature with visible signage at the driveway entrance so arriving responders are aware of it.
• Trim dense vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain clear vehicle passage and sightlines for approaching responders.
• Thin dense vegetation between the residence and detached structure to keep a clear path between the two buildings for responder movement on foot.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the walkway so responders can move quickly between the front and rear of the property.
• Mark or post the rear access limitation at the driveway entrance so responders know rear vehicle access is not available before committing to an approach.
• Keep a gate, gap, or marked foot path through rear vegetation so responders can reach the back of the property on foot.
• Identify and mark the nearest hydrant or static water source on the property sign at the street to assist the first arriving engine company.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create open space between the trees and the building.
• Separate scattered trees from each other by removing low-hanging branches and any shrubs growing between them.
• Trim or remove vegetation that is growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Clear grass and low ground cover within several feet of the structure's base.
• Keep grass areas mowed short, particularly where grass cover connects open areas to the structure.
• Remove any dead grass, leaves, or plant debris that has collected near the structure or along its foundation.
• Thin shrubs and plants growing between the tree cluster and the structure to open the space between them.
• Keep low branches on scattered trees trimmed up from the ground to reduce the chance of fire moving from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Maintain clear vehicle access along all available routes to the structure by keeping branches trimmed back from the travel surface.
• Mark or keep visible the access route entrances so they remain easy to identify from the road.
• Remove any plant material or debris that has accumulated near the water feature's edges if it is close to the structure.
• Keep the areas between open green space and the structure free of dense low-growing plants that could carry fire toward the building.
